div.p: Proclamation to Japan, July 26, 1945 and Department Policy

row.cell: 1.Unconditional Surrender
“Unconditional Surrender of all Japanese armed forces”.
Unconditional Surrender of Japan—Government and armed forces.
2.Terms
Japan is given an opportunity to end this war on the basis of stated terms.
Japan must obey all directives which may be given by the Allied powers. The powers, however, should announce in advance their basic policies in regard to Japan.
3.Legal Powers of Allies in Japan
Designated points in Japan to be occupied. Authority outside of these points is left uncertain.
The Allies to take over the government of Japan and to possess supreme authority.
4.The Japanese Government
The status of the Japanese Government is left uncertain. It apparently is to continue and to exercise certain functions. (Article 10).
All authority of the Japanese Government is transferred to the Allies. Administrative machinery and most agencies to function under direction of Allies.
5.The Emperor
No mention. Since his removal is not stipulated, it may be assumed that he may remain.
The Emperor is to sign and announce the unconditional surrender of Japan. His powers pass to the Allies. He is to be held in protective custody.
6.Objectives

Irresponsible militarism and Japan’s war-making power to be destroyed. Freedom of speech, of religion, and of thought, and respect for fundamental rights. Establishment of a peacefully inclined and responsible government.
No important differences.
7.Enforcement of Objectives

Not clear. The Japanese Government has the responsibility of carrying out some and possibly all the demands of the Allies. Some of the “terms” would seem to necessitate direct action by Allied authorities.
The Allies’ Government in Japan will, itself, enforce its demands.
8.Economic Provisions
Japan to maintain industries necessary to sustain her economy and pay reparations. Industries to be demilitarized.
No important differences.
9.Loss of Territories
Cairo Declaration. Japanese sovereignty to be limited to four main islands “and such minor islands as we determine”.
No Department Policy beyond the Cairo Declaration.
10.Withdrawal of Occupation Forces
As soon as stated objectives of Allies have been accomplished and a peacefully inclined and responsible government is established.
No definite provisions.
